name: level1-playthrough-revolt
description: Level 1 worker revolt scenario: no well-being buildings and a 12-strong crew drilling flat out crash wellBeing to its floor, and the site revolts. #1313: the mine freezes the moment the level ends, so the scenario funds the level ($1,050,000) to stay solvent -- bankruptcy used to fire mid-drill at tick 209 and the file ticked on over an already-lost game -- and reaches the revolt as the first and only end (tick 383). Everything after it asserts the frozen state.

steps.description: #553: staffed:true hires and equips, for free, employee #1 driller (blasting lvl1, driving.drill_rig lvl1) through #5 driver, plus vehicles #1 drill_rig through #4 rock_fragmenter (all unmanned). Cost is free -- does not change starting cash. The file's own 7 hand-hired employees below become #6-#12.

#553: staffed:true does NOT auto-assign a driver -- the free drill_rig (vehicle #1) is still a mesh nobody can drive until employee #1, the only qualified driller on the roster at this point, boards it. #921: Fleet panel's Assign/Unassign controls removed; vehicles are now claimed automatically by a qualified employee when a vehicle-gated task needs one, so this step runs as a direct bootstrap primitive instead of a click.

#553 sandbox-measured finding: staffed:true parks its 4 vehicles in a row at (0,2)/(2,2)/(4,2)/(6,2), and on dusty_hollow's terrain that row sits inside the map's only ramp corridor out of the spawn corner -- tickVehicleOnNavGrid recomputes the same A* path every tick (avoidVehicles:false) and only refuses the immediate next cell if another vehicle already occupies it (isCellOccupiedByOtherVehicle), so the drill_rig (vehicle #1) advances exactly one cell to (1,2) and then waits forever behind the unmanned debris_hauler parked at (2,2) -- confirmed by direct trace: 40+ ticks stuck at (1,2), waitingTicks climbing, holeCount never leaving 0. This file never uses a debris_hauler, rock_digger or rock_fragmenter (zero hauling/fragment-breaking anywhere in its script), so scrapping the blocker -- and the other two idle vehicles that would otherwise just draw maintenance upkeep for nothing -- clears the corridor and turns dead weight into cash. #929: opens the Fleet panel itself. The step that used to open it with a real toolbar click became a bootstrap command under #921, and UIManager only updates a visible panel -- a Fleet panel nobody opened renders no vehicle cards at all, so this click had nothing to land on.
rock_digger #3 was never in the drill_rig's path, but this file has no use for it either -- scrapped for the same reason as #2: pure upkeep with nothing to show for it.

rock_fragmenter #4, same reasoning. Sandbox-measured residual proceeds across all three scraps ($10,000 + $20,000 + $12,800 = $42,800) fund the 7 hires below without touching the $50,000 opening balance.
#553: this and the following 6 hires are the file's own original crew, renumbered #6-#12 now that staffed:true claims #1-#5 first.

#553: employee #7. Deliberately left unlicensed for driving.drill_rig -- sandbox-measured, licensing this driller as a backup only adds a second casualty to blast 1 (they end up standing near the pattern too) without changing the outcome, since patterns 2-4 stall on the missing vehicle regardless of how many licensed drillers are left alive (see the note on the pattern-2 drill_plan step below).

Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:4 cols:4 spacing:3 depth:6 start:6,5

expect.note: #553: confirming the grid only orders the 16 holes -- they're ghosts until employee #1 drives vehicle #1 to each one, drained by the tick-wait steps below.

steps.description: #1151: shifted one cell east. Under the 30-degree slope gate (5,11) sits outside the crew's climb-reachable patch on dusty_hollow, so no driller could ever claim that hole and the pattern stalled at 15 of 16 forever. Measured by replaying this file's own steps to this point; start:6,5 is the nearest origin whose whole 4x4 grid is reachable.

expect.note: #596/#597-followup: setupEvents idempotency + the cooldown-threshold caching fix change exactly when the first random event goes pending -- this 283-tick request now advances 165 ticks (not 115) before stopping, landing 10 of 16 holes, and the event that fires is a different one too (union_unlucky_days, not weather_minor_tremor -- #596's event-pool dedup change reorders the RNG draw). tickCount/holeCount/orderedHoleCount/wellBeing converted from chained absolutes to directional (issue #596): exactly how far a tick request gets before an event interrupts it is what these two fixes changed, so pinning a fresh absolute here just repeats the same fragility under the next timing-affecting fix. ecology/safety/nuisance/deathCount/bankrupt/levelEnded are untouched by the event-timing shift and stay exact.

steps.description: #596/#597-followup: this event is now union_unlucky_days, not weather_minor_tremor -- #596's event-pool dedup fix changed the RNG draw order for which event becomes eligible first. Option 0 ("Lucky Charms") is a fixed, RNG-free delta sandbox-traced to cashDelta:-2000, scoreDelta.wellBeing:+5 -- no safety effect, unlike the old weather_minor_tremor draw. tickCount dropped from this step's own expect: it doesn't move during an event-choose (no ticking happens here), and the tick-283 step above already covers it directionally.

expect.note: #596/#597-followup: this 168-tick request completes in full (175->343, all 168 ticks). #1313: the level is funded so payroll never reaches the $5,000 bankruptcy threshold (it used to, at tick 209, and the file kept ticking over an ended level -- a frozen mine no longer allows that); the level is still running here. wellBeing crashes to 0 during this stretch (fatigue collapse with no living quarters anywhere in this file) and its zero streak, which started at tick 263, is what ends the level in the revolt below.

steps.description: #1313: advance until the level ends. REVOLT_TICKS (120 consecutive ticks at wellBeing<=0, WorkerRevolt.ts) elapse at tick 383 and the mine freezes there -- earlier than any blast could land (a blaster needs more than 40 ticks to charge the 16 holes), so this file ends in a revolt with the pattern drilled and never fired.
#1313: the level has ended in a revolt with no hole charged, so there is nothing to fire: the console refuses, nothing dies, and the level-end screen covers the execute control.

expect.note: #1313: frozen mine -- a tick after the end advances nothing, cash and tickCount stay put.

steps.description: #1313: read-only state after the revolt: nobody died (no blast ever fired) and the crew is intact.

expect.note: final state: the revolt at tick 383 is the level's only end, and the mine stayed frozen after it. #1313.

steps.description: #1313: final campaign status -- still the revolt, still tick 383.
